summary.done: Created petal-panic/js/terrain.js: a pure terrain grammar + seeded per-game RNG. createRng(seed) is a mulberry32 PRNG (numeric or FNV-1a-hashed string seed) with next/int/pick/float, so the same seed always yields the identical generation stream. BLOCK (1w, heights 1/2/3, solid, ground-rising, not one-way) and PLATFORM (widths 1/2/3, tiers 1/2/3, one-way, one thickness, not solid) grammars + makeBlock/makePlatform factories. doubleJumpReach/minHeroDoubleJumpReach/maxClearableStep derive tier spacing from the real hero physics (GRAVITY 1500, double-jump 0.85 factor, Balthazar is the binding weaker jumper) so each tier step is reachable by both heroes with a 16px margin; tierToOffset maps tiers 0..3 to equal-spaced pixel offsets. Added terrain.test.js (21 tests).
summary.decisions: mulberry32 for the PRNG (small, deterministic, platform-stable). Tier spacing is derived from hero reach by construction rather than a hand-tuned constant, so the 'reachable by both heroes' invariant holds automatically; Balthazar (smaller jump) is the binding constraint. Units model (not pixels) so 3.2 owns pixel layout. RNG is a stateful closure; determinism comes from fixed seed.

summary.lessons_learned: The vertical composer's axis-length-based stacking (axisPos += axisLen) was the root cause of the unreachable inter-macro join: the axis length includes entryClear + exitClear breathing room, so the next macro's first platform ends up entryClear + firstLocalTier tiers above the previous macro's peak. The fix is to anchor the next macro's first platform to a reachable elevation (prevPeak + MAX_ELEVATION_STEP) rather than blindly stacking at axisPos. The validation was also blind to inter-macro joins — it only checked within-macro steps. The fix is to check the step from the previous macro's PEAK to the next macro's FIRST platform when placementIds differ.
summary.done: Fixed both MAJOR findings from R2 review. (MAJOR 1 / R2 #2): The vertical composer now ensures reachable inter-macro joins. Added firstPlatformAbsY() and lastPlatformAbsY() helpers to compute a macro's first/peak platform elevation in absolute climb space. In composeArea's vertical placement loop, track prevPeakAbsY (the previous macro's peak elevation); before placing the next macro, if its natural first-platform elevation (axisPos + firstLocalTier) would exceed prevPeakAbsY + MAX_ELEVATION_STEP, shift the macro DOWN so its first platform sits at exactly prevPeakAbsY + MAX_ELEVATION_STEP. This eliminates the unreachable 4-tier gap (e.g. seed 1 previously: macro 0 peak y=3, macro 1 first y=7 → now: macro 0 peak y=3, macro 1 first y=4). Updated validateLayout to CHECK inter-macro vertical transitions: when two consecutive platforms have different placementIds, compute the step from the previous macro's PEAK (max y of all platforms in that macro) to the current macro's first platform; if the upward step exceeds MAX_ELEVATION_STEP, throw 'unreachable join'. Also added 2 new tests: one that asserts an unreachable inter-macro join (4-tier gap) throws, and one that asserts a reachable join (1-tier step) passes. (MAJOR 2 / R2 #2): The horizontal zone bounds now match the terrain budget. Added ZONE_WIDTH_HORIZONTAL=4000 (2x the ~2000px prototype segment) and ZONE_WIDTH_VERTICAL=1600 (one screen, for vertical + boss zones). buildLevelZones now uses the orientation-aware width: horizontal zones are 4000px wide, vertical zones stay 1600px wide (one screen per structure.md §4), and the boss zone stays 1600px (fixed-size arena). ZONE_EXIT_X is now derived from the zone's actual width (bounds.w - ZONE_EXIT_PAD) so the exit flag scales with the zone. Added ZONE_WIDTH (backward-compat alias = 1600) and ZONE_EXIT_X (backward-compat alias = 1480). Added a new zone test asserting horizontal zones are ZONE_WIDTH_HORIZONTAL wide and vertical/boss zones are ZONE_WIDTH_VERTICAL wide.
summary.decisions: (1) Inter-macro join fix: shift the next macro DOWN (not up) so its first platform is at prevPeak + MAX_ELEVATION_STEP. Shifting down is safer (never exceeds the budget) and the macro's subsequent platforms (higher tiers) continue the climb naturally. (2) Validation: the inter-macro check uses the previous macro's PEAK (max y of all its platforms) as the reference, not the previous platform in sort order. This is correct because the hero stands on the highest platform of the previous macro before jumping to the next. (3) Zone width: horizontal zones are 4000px wide (2x prototype segment), vertical zones stay 1600px (one screen per structure.md §4), boss zone stays 1600px (fixed-size arena). The zone IS the world (structure.md §2) — the terrain fills the zone, and the zone is the terrain's container. (4) ZONE_EXIT_X is now derived from bounds.w - ZONE_EXIT_PAD so it scales with the zone's width. Backward-compat aliases (ZONE_WIDTH, ZONE_EXIT_X) are kept for existing consumers.
summary.tradeoffs: The vertical composer's shift-down logic can cause macros to overlap in the y-axis when the budget is tight (e.g. two climbing macros with entryClear=2 each: macro 0 at y=0-6, macro 1 shifted to y=3-9, overlapping y=3-6). This is acceptable because the platforms are one-way (pass-through from below) so the hero can still reach the higher platforms; the overlap is a visual artifact, not a gameplay blocker. The inter-macro validation is the authoritative check — if a join is unreachable, it throws. For the horizontal zone width change: the exit flag x is now derived from bounds.w - ZONE_EXIT_PAD instead of a hardcoded ZONE_EXIT_X=1480. This is a behavior change for any code that reads ZONE_EXIT_X directly (it still works for vertical/boss zones at 1480, but horizontal zones now put the exit at 3880). The ZONE_EXIT_X export is kept as a backward-compat alias for the 1600px width.

summary.decisions: 1) Kept the resolver pure (no DOM, no entity construction) and placed it in macros.js next to the composer — it consumes the layout the composer produces and emits plain {slot,x,y,type} descriptors, leaving entity instantiation to a later task. 2) Kept quantity budget and placement/type chance strictly distinct (populate.md §1): the budget is the requested count; slot selection is a seeded Fisher-Yates prefix (no independent coin flips, so a fixed budget never yields an accidental empty area when slots exist), and type assignment is a separate weighted draw capped per type. 3) Under-placement (slots < budget) is surfaced via a budgets report ({requested,placed,slots}) rather than hidden or over-filled — matching the doc's 'revise the composition rather than pile items into invalid positions'. 4) Barrel chain threshold (BARREL_CHAIN_MAX_UNITS) is derived from the real BARREL_DEF.explosion.radius (120px) and barrel footprint (32px) via UNIT_PX, not a hand-tuned literal, so the chain claim is grounded in the actual blast area. 5) Explosive barrels are ordered to chainable slots first so they sit in the middle of a structure (satisfying chain), not isolated at its edges. 6) Did NOT modify generateLevel()/randomPositions() in level.js (runtime still on the deprecated legacy corridor; rewiring it to the zone+population engine is a later task) — the resolver is the drop-in the zone engine will call, per the snippet's blueprint. 7) BLOCKER fix (task 4.1 re-review): slot y is now the supporting surface elevation (surfaceElevationAt walks the macro's own unit sequence and returns block height / platform tier / ground 0), so items rest ON TOP of solids, never inside them. The resolver also runs a defense-in-depth slotIsOnValidSurface check against the layout's block AABBs and throws if any slot is inside a solid. 8) Barrel constants (BARREL_PX, BARREL_EXPLOSION_RADIUS_PX) now import BARREL_DEF from object.js instead of duplicating 32/120 magic numbers. 9) classifyBarrelStructure now returns a new "small" category for 2-3 barrels (medium is strictly 4-9 per populate.md §3). 10) Macro slot vocabulary expanded: each macro now declares 3-4 enemy, 2-3 barrel, 1-2 powerup slots so typical budgets can be met. 11) populationSnapshot() added — a stable, value-only deep copy of the population for storage/restoration (restoreArea integration deferred to task 7.1).

summary.lessons_learned: The 'never in solids' acceptance clause is only as good as the macro slot authoring: several task-3.2 slots are placed on block units, so items placed on them sit in solids. The resolver is correct (it places only on declared slots); the defect is in the slot x's. When verifying 'on a valid slot', match items to slots by (x, y, slot.type) — the item's own  field is the enemy/powerup name, not the slot type, so a naive key on item.type will false-positive. The slot x coordinate in a macro placement is the offset from the entry-clear-zone START (not the macro start), so surfaceElevationAt must walk units from cursor=0, not cursor=entryClear. A ±0.5 cell overlap check in slotIsOnValidSurface false-positives against adjacent unit cells — use exact unit-aligned x-range containment instead.

MAJOR (R2 #3): macro slot vocabulary expanded to 3-4 enemy / 2-3 barrel / 1-2 powerup per macro; under-placement still surfaced via the budgets report. MAJOR (R2 #4): populationSnapshot() added as a stable value-only snapshot for storage/restore (restoreArea wiring deferred to task 7.1, noted in comments).
